solutionSource.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

entries.clue: Snug wearing little tunic (6)

indicatorNotes.wearing: the little word has the snug on, round its middle

blocks.note: a tad is a little bit; BAR goes between TA and D
a snug is a small cosy bar room in a British pub

annotation.surface: Someone cosy in a skimpy little top.
annotation.walkthrough: Snug reads as an adjective for a tight tunic, but it is the noun: the snug is a small private room in a British pub.
annotation.definitionFit: A tabard is a sleeveless tunic, worn by heralds or over armour.

entries.clue: Staff do up house (5)

indicatorNotes.up: in a down clue, up turns the letters to read from the bottom

blocks.note: a rod is a staff or stick
ut is the old name for do, the first note of the scale

annotation.surface: An order to the staff to decorate the house.
annotation.walkthrough: Staff looks like employees and do up like redecorating; UT is the older name for the note do.
annotation.definitionFit: The Tudors were the royal house of Henry VIII and Elizabeth I.

entries.clue: The worst drink for your health (7,2)

annotation.definition: The worst drink for your health

blocks.note: the surface wants the least healthy option; the setter means the bottoms, the lowest of the low
not a drink that is good for you but a toast, as in drinking to your health

annotation.surface: A doctor's warning about the unhealthiest thing you can drink.
annotation.walkthrough: The worst are the bottoms, and to drink to someone's health you say this toast; the clue reads as a health warning instead.
annotation.definitionFit: Bottoms up is a toast said when drinking to someone's health.

entries.clue: Ladder on a car (8)

blocks.note: a ladder in tights is a run
a talk on something is a talk about it

annotation.surface: A ladder strapped to a car roof.
annotation.walkthrough: The ladder is the British word for a run in tights or stockings.
annotation.definitionFit: A runabout is a small car for short local trips.

entries.clue: Like Wagner’s Ring, a chaotic Act I (8)

indicatorNotes.chaotic: ACT I is thrown into disorder

blocks.note: a ring is O-shaped
a pound a head is a pound per head
the letters of ACT I, jumbled

annotation.surface: A critic judging the opening act of a Ring production a shambles.
annotation.walkthrough: Wagner's Ring pulls the whole phrase together, but the definition stops at Wagner's and Ring is just O; the plain a is PER, as in so much a head.
annotation.definitionFit: Wagner's works are operas, so something like Wagner's is operatic.

entries.clue: Sewer needs sign when circulation is impeded (4,3,7)

blocks.note: a sewer here is someone who sews, and these are the tools of the trade
the tingling in a limb when its blood supply is cut off

annotation.surface: A drainage engineer diagnosing a blocked sewer.
annotation.walkthrough: Sewer reads as a drain, with circulation as its flow; it is one who sews, whose kit is pins and needles.
annotation.definitionFit: Both senses are literal: pins and needles are what a sewer works with, and the phrase also names the tingling felt when blood flow to a limb is cut off.

entries.clue: I’m afraid boring leftie was humming (6)

indicatorNotes.boring: the cry drills into the leftie

blocks.note: a red is a left-winger; EEK goes between R and ED
eek! is a cry of fright

annotation.surface: An apology for finding a left-wing speaker dull.
annotation.walkthrough: I'm afraid reads as a polite apology but is the scared cry EEK, and boring means drilling into, not dull; humming is British slang for smelling bad.
annotation.definitionFit: Humming is British slang for smelling strongly, so was humming means reeked.

entries.clue: Rwandan boy king one’s raised (5)

indicatorNotes.raised: in a down clue, raised turns the letters to read upwards

blocks.note: Tutankhamun, the boy king of Egypt, is Tut for short
one is I, and one's is one is, so I + S

annotation.surface: A young African prince being lifted up in celebration.
annotation.walkthrough: The boy king is Tutankhamun, not a Rwandan; the one's reads as a possessive but is one is, I plus S.
annotation.definitionFit: The Tutsi are one of the main peoples of Rwanda, so a Tutsi can be a Rwandan.

entries.clue: Religious type just about runs gym (9)

indicatorNotes.about: the word for just goes around the others

blocks.note: clean as in clean forgot, i.e. just, completely; R GYM goes between CLE and AN
r is the cricket abbreviation for runs
as written

annotation.surface: A pious sort who only jogs around the gym.
annotation.walkthrough: Just about reads as barely, but just is CLEAN and about wraps it round the rest.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by category: a clergyman is an ordained minister, one sort of religious type.

entries.clue: Chaos in naming arrested suspect (14)

indicatorNotes.suspect: the letters are not to be trusted in their order

blocks.note: the fourteen letters rearranged

annotation.surface: Uproar as police name the person they have detained.
annotation.walkthrough: Arrested suspect reads as a detained person, but suspect is the anagram signal and arrested is fodder.
annotation.definitionFit: A disarrangement is a state of disorder, which is chaos.

entries.clue: Can refugees stay in north, perhaps? (9,6)

blocks.note: a can is slang for a prison, and asylum seekers can be held in one
read the answer as an instruction: the middle letter of detention is N, and N is north

annotation.surface: A question about whether refugees are allowed to remain in the north of the country.
annotation.walkthrough: Can reads as may, but it is a noun: a can is a prison. The second half reads the answer as a clue in itself, with perhaps flagging north as one example of an N.
annotation.definitionFit: Can is slang for a prison, the kind where refugees are held; north, perhaps, is the letter N, which the answer describes as the centre of DETENTION.

entries.clue: House doctor supplied with right lozenge (5)

blocks.note: R = right
ho. is the abbreviation for house
MB, Bachelor of Medicine, is a doctor's degree

annotation.surface: A GP on a home visit handing out throat sweets.
annotation.walkthrough: Lozenge reads as a throat sweet, but here it is the diamond shape.
annotation.definitionFit: A rhomb, or rhombus, is a diamond shape, which is what a lozenge is in geometry and heraldry.

entries.clue: Stripped naked in shelter, causing arousal (9)

indicatorNotes.in: the stripped word goes inside the shelter

blocks.note: an awning is a canopy shelter; AKE goes between AW and NING
naked without its first and last letters

annotation.surface: Someone undressed under a canopy, stirring desire.
annotation.walkthrough: Stripped naked is a doubled image of nudity, but stripped works on the word naked, peeling off N and D.
annotation.definitionFit: An awakening experience is one that rouses, so awakening means causing arousal.

entries.clue: Ball formed out of bent square (10)

indicatorNotes.bent: square is twisted out of shape
indicatorNotes.out of: formed sits outside the bent word

blocks.note: formed = made; SQUERA goes between MA and DE
the letters of square, bent

annotation.surface: A round object moulded from a crooked cube.
annotation.walkthrough: Ball and square set up a geometry puzzle, but the ball is a dance.
annotation.definitionFit: A masquerade is a ball where guests wear masks.

entries.clue: City cat given bowl coated in gold (9)

indicatorNotes.coated in: the bowl gets a covering of gold round it

blocks.note: mog is British slang for a cat
Au is the chemical symbol for gold; DISH goes between A and U
a bowl is a dish

annotation.surface: A pampered town cat served its food in a gilded bowl.
annotation.walkthrough: Mog, or moggy, is British slang for an ordinary cat.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: this is the capital of Somalia, on the Indian Ocean coast.

entries.clue: Keep sending plans over (4)

indicatorNotes.over: the plans are turned over, end to end

blocks.note: maps are plans, as of a town

annotation.surface: Someone who keeps posting designs back and forth.
annotation.walkthrough: Plans reads as intentions; here they are drawn maps.
annotation.definitionFit: A modern verb from junk email, named after the tinned meat: it means sending the same unwanted message again and again.

entries.clue: Ancient chief wrong to be quoted (9)

indicatorNotes.to be quoted: the phrase is spoken, so heard not spelt

blocks.note: prime = chief, evil = wrong; said together they sound like the answer

annotation.surface: An old tribal leader whose misdeeds are about to be cited.
annotation.walkthrough: Chief reads as a tribal leader in an ancient scene, but it is the adjective prime.
annotation.definitionFit: Primaeval means belonging to the earliest ages, which is ancient.

entries.clue: The best medicine that may be canned (8)

blocks.note: from the proverb that it is the best medicine
the canned kind is recorded audience noise on a TV comedy soundtrack

annotation.surface: A remedy so good it could be sold in tins.
annotation.walkthrough: Both halves are stock phrases: laughter is the best medicine, and canned laughter is recorded on a TV sitcom's soundtrack.
annotation.definitionFit: The first sense is a proverb and the second an idiom, canned laughter being pre-recorded audience noise.

entries.clue: Open wide space, originally empty (4)

blocks.note: a gap is a space
first letter of empty

annotation.surface: A description of vast empty land, bare from the start.
annotation.walkthrough: Open wide space reads as a single landscape, but open wide is the verb and space is a gap.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym, used of mouths, wounds and chasms that stand wide open.

entries.clue: Seizure occurs when an old flame’s in a state (10)

indicatorNotes.in: the old flame sits inside a state

blocks.note: as written
a state is a nation; EX goes between N and ATION
an old flame is an ex

annotation.surface: Someone having a fit because a former lover is in a flap.
annotation.walkthrough: Seizure suggests a fit and in a state suggests agitation; both are political here, a territory taken and a country.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym from politics: one state's seizure of another's territory, as with Crimea in 2014.

entries.clue: Weak yet effective, somewhat upset (6)

indicatorNotes.somewhat: only part of the phrase is used
indicatorNotes.upset: in a down clue, upset turns the letters to read upwards

blocks.note: the letters run backwards across the end of yet and the start of effective

annotation.surface: Someone feeble yet somehow getting results, if a little upset.
annotation.walkthrough: The weak-but-effective contrast reads as the whole idea, but yET EFFEctive holds ETEFFE, which read upwards is the answer.
annotation.definitionFit: Effete means weak, lacking vigour.

entries.clue: Head of school retired? Define “sacked” (4-5)

indicatorNotes.retired: the school goes back, reading right to left
indicatorNotes.sacked: the letters of define are shaken up, as a place is sacked

blocks.note: a school of whales or dolphins is a pod
define, sacked

annotation.surface: A dictionary entry: what does it mean for a retired headteacher to be fired?
annotation.walkthrough: Head of school reads as a headteacher, but Head alone is the definition, drug slang as in pothead; school is a pod of whales.
annotation.definitionFit: A head, as in pothead or acidhead, is a drug user, and a dope-fiend is a drug addict.

entries.clue: Tip for new head of government (5)

blocks.note: pro = for, in favour of
N = new
first letter of government

annotation.surface: Advice passed to an incoming prime minister.
annotation.walkthrough: Tip reads as a piece of advice, and head of government as a leader; tip is a point and head of only the first letter.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: the pointed ends of a fork are its prongs, each one a tip.

entries.clue: Old king, also regal (5)

blocks.note: GR, Georgius Rex, is the cipher of the King Georges
also = and

annotation.surface: A former monarch described as properly majestic.
annotation.walkthrough: GR stands for Georgius Rex, King George, and appears on British postboxes of those reigns.
annotation.definitionFit: Grand and regal both mean magnificent and stately.

entries.clue: Fit detective shot (5)

blocks.note: DI = detective inspector
a shy is a throw or shot, as at a coconut shy

annotation.surface: A police officer fit enough to be gunned down, or worn out.
annotation.walkthrough: Fit and dishy are both British slang for good-looking; a coconut shy is a fairground stall where you throw at coconuts.
annotation.definitionFit: Fit and dishy are both British slang for attractive.

entries.clue: Shop workers paid for shopping (5,10)

blocks.note: they are employed in a store
to shop someone is British slang for informing on them, and these staff are paid to report shoplifters

annotation.surface: Retail staff who get paid to go shopping.
annotation.walkthrough: Paid for shopping sounds like a dream job buying things, but to shop someone is British slang for turning them in.
annotation.definitionFit: Both are literal descriptions of one job: working in a store, catching shoplifters and shopping them to the police.

entries.clue: A French restroom full of posh lotions (8)

indicatorNotes.full of: the restroom holds the posh letter

blocks.note: un is French for a
the gents is a men's toilet; U goes between G and ENTS
U means upper-class, as opposed to non-U

annotation.surface: A smart French washroom stocked with expensive creams.
annotation.walkthrough: The gents is the British men's toilet, and U is the old label for upper-class usage.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym, if a rather formal one, from the Latin for ointment: soothing salves rubbed on the skin.

entries.clue: Recover after nil by mouth (6)

blocks.note: nil = 0, O
to rally is to recover

annotation.surface: A patient recovering after being kept nil by mouth before surgery.
annotation.walkthrough: Nil by mouth is the hospital instruction not to eat or drink, which hides the split: nil is O and by mouth is the definition.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym from medicine, where a drug to be taken by mouth is labelled as taken orally.
